llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: The API key and profile-data concern is valid user guidance, but authenticated access to email, credits, and study stats is documented and purpose-aligned for an account-based study integration.
[SQP-2] expected: The external-transmission concern is a documentation gap rather than hidden behavior: README.md and SKILL.md repeatedly describe an EchoDecks External API integration, and generation features necessarily send topic/text or deck data to that service.
[SQP-2] expected: The state-changing operations are purpose-aligned and named directly, including deck creation, card generation, podcast generation, and review submission; clearer read/write labeling would improve user control.
[VirusTotal telemetry] expected: VirusTotal reported clean results and described the script as a constrained EchoDecks client; the high-entropy/eval note was not supported by artifact evidence of eval, obfuscation, persistence, or arbitrary execution.
llm.guidance: Install only if you trust EchoDecks with the study materials, deck data, review activity, and account details involved in your requests. Keep ECHODECKS_API_KEY private, do not paste secrets or regulated data into generation inputs, and remember that generation/review actions may change your EchoDecks account and consume credits.
llm.summary: This is a straightforward EchoDecks API skill, with privacy and credential-handling caveats users should understand before use.

All API calls are well-defined and constrained by `argparse` arguments, preventing arbitrary command execution or data exfiltration beyond the stated purpose.
